records.notes: Pass-128 check (2026-10-10): UNAVAILABLE: identity not established. Sources conflict on configuration: an active 4-way with servo (6 ohm, 86 dB, 25-32 kHz) versus a passive 5-way (4 ohm, 25-32 kHz). The RS-1B revision cannot be fixed from the catalog row, so no values are transferred. Pass-136 correction: the pass-128 UNAVAILABLE label is reverted to UNVERIFIED because no exact RS-1B identity ledger entry exists for this row; no values are assigned from either conflicting configuration. Pass-136 check (2026-10-10): Secondary sources conflict on the RS-1B configuration: vintagetechnologyarchive.com describes a 1985 four-way active servo system (6 Ω, 86 dB, 25 Hz–32 kHz, 400 W); hifi-guide.com describes a passive five-way (4 Ω, 25–32 kHz). The infinity-classics.de RS_1B_technical_sheet.pdf URL returned 404 on this pass. No manufacturer RS-1B sheet was reached, so no values are stored and the record stays UNVERIFIED. Pass-138 check (2026-10-10): The Harman support owner's manual (part 333365-001) covers the Reference Standard RS 1, RS 2 and RS 3 bookshelf models and does not include the RS-1B. A vintagetechnologyarchive RS-1B (1985) entry describes an active four-way system with 6 ohm, 86 dB, 25 Hz-32 kHz and 400 W, which conflicts with the earlier passive five-way copy. Single third-party source (vintagetechnologyarchive.com, RS-1B 1985). Its own description is internally inconsistent (a four-way active system with crossovers at 150/800 Hz and 3.5 kHz in the text, versus 150/700 Hz/3 kHz/8 kHz in the spec list), so driverCount, crossover and response fields are not stored. The 400 W power handling has no stated definition and is not stored. The RS 1 passive copy (hifi-guide.com, 8 ohm, 89 dB) and the RS 1.5 technical sheet are different models and are not used. Pass-140 (2026-10-10): third-party tier applied to the single-source RS-1B values. Owner decision (2026-10-12): the unverified single-source values (86 dB sensitivity, 6 ohm impedance, 12 in woofer, all from https://vintagetechnologyarchive.com/audio/infinity/rs-1b/) are cleared to UNAVAILABLE. The configuration conflict with the hifi-guide.com passive five-way copy is unresolved, and the row stays in the dataset. overallStatus is UNVERIFIED because no sourced field remains.

Pass-128 check (2026-10-10): Manufacturer page not located. Secondary sources conflict across generations (1 or 4 ohm wiring, earlier vs later production, Scintilla vs Scintilla Signature); none transferred. Pass-130 check (2026-10-10): secondary sources conflict and are revision-dependent. hifi-advice.com gives 20 Hz (-6 dB)–25 kHz, 79 dB at 3 m and 1 or 4 Ω (1 Ω only after 1996). audio-database.com gives 30 Hz–25 kHz and 1 or 4 Ω. hifi-wiki describes a Scintilla Signature (±3 dB 25 Hz–20 kHz). No manufacturer source was reached. Pass-136 check (2026-10-10): Secondary sources describe impedance variants by production period (1 or 4 Ω early; 1 Ω only later) and quote different sensitivity values for the two (79 dB at 4 Ω and 85 dB at 1 Ω on one site; 79 dB/W·m on a hifi-wiki Signature entry). A separate Scintilla Signature is also described. No single revision is established for the catalog row, so no values are stored.

Pass-128 check (2026-10-10): Only Autograph MINI (MINI-OW) data was located and is not transferable. The full Autograph official page was not located. Pass-130 check (2026-10-10): sources found cover the Tannoy Autograph MINI only (88 dB 2.83 V/1 m, 8 Ω, 68 Hz–54 kHz; 106 Hz–20 kHz ±3 dB). The full Autograph is not covered, and Mini data must not be transferred. Pass-135 check (2026-10-10): the tannoy.com guessed product URL returned a 404. Autograph MINI sources (hifiengine, avstore, theaudiospecialists) carry the Mini's 106 Hz–20 kHz ±3 dB and 85–88 dB figures; they are not transferable to the full Autograph. No full Autograph manufacturer page was reached. Pass-136 check (2026-10-10): A third-party specification page labels its record "AUTOGRAPH MINI-OW" and links a Tannoy modelCode for the Mini-OW (106 Hz–20 kHz ±3 dB, 85 dB at 1 W/1 m, 8 Ω). These are the Mini values, which are not transferred. The catalog row "Autograph" does not say whether it is the Mini or the full-size model, and no full-size Autograph manufacturer page was reached.

Pass-128 check (2026-10-10): Only Sonance Mariner MX62 and MX66 retailer pages were found; these are not the exact 'Mariner 6' catalog row. No values transferred. Pass-130 check (2026-10-10): retailer listings describe different Sonance Mariner models (Mariner MX66, 6-1/2-inch 2-way outdoor), with conflicting specs (50 Hz–20 kHz ±3 dB vs 55 Hz–20 kHz; 89 vs 90 dB; 8 vs 6 Ω). The Mariner 6 record's exact variant is not established. Pass-135 check (2026-10-10): the sonance.com product URL guess returned a 404 page and the site is blocked for the fetch tool. Retailer copies (Abt, Best Buy, auditorium.de) describe the MX62 (6.5 in, 2-way, 55 Hz–20 kHz ±3 dB, 89 dB SPL 2.83 V/1 m, 8 Ω nominal / 6 Ω minimum, operating power 5–125 W) and the MX66 (50 Hz–20 kHz ±3 dB, 90 dB, same impedance). Both are described as '6-inch' outdoor speakers, so 'Mariner 6' does not establish which catalog row is meant. Neither set of values is transferred. Pass-136 check (2026-10-10): Sonance's page for product 93608 is the Mariner MX62 (6.5 in woofer, 1 in tweeter, 55 Hz–20 kHz ±3 dB, 89 dB at 2.83 V/1 m, 8 Ω nominal). A Best Buy listing for "Mariner 6-1/2" (model MARINER 61) gives different values (0.75 in tweeter, 80 W maximum). The MX66 is a further model. The catalog row "Mariner 6" does not identify which of these it is, so none is transferred.

A resale listing describes a "TB2" (40 Hz–25 kHz, 90 dB, 150 W peak). The TB2, TB2+ and TB2S+ revisions conflict and the catalog row does not name one, so no values are stored. Pass-138 check (2026-10-10): The PMC iSeries TB2i datasheet (2012, pmc-speakers.com) lists several models in one table (response rows from 19 Hz to 50 Hz low ends, 87-90 dB at 1 W/1 m, 4-8 ohm, 2 kHz and 380 Hz/3.8 kHz crossovers). The model names of the columns are not visible in the copy reached, so no column is assigned to the bare TB2. Nothing stored. Pass-144 (2026-10-11): pmc-speakers.com archive page for TB2 (https://pmc-speakers.com/products/archive/archive/tb2/) was opened; its Specifications tab did not render in the fetched text, so no value could be read from it. The pmc-speakers.com TB2S+ page is a different revision and was not used. Secondary listings (reverb.com, avforums.com) give 90 dB, 8 Ω and 40 Hz–25 kHz for the TB2; they are not stored because they cannot be tied to this record's revision. No change to fields.

The revision is still not resolved for this record, so no value is stored. A lower limit alone is not a field. Pass-137 check (2026-10-10): the PMC archive page for BB5 XBD (manufacturer, undated, c.2011) lists drive units LF 2×380 mm, MF 75 mm, HF 34 mm, crossover 380 Hz / 3.8 kHz, amplifier LF 900 W, MF 300 W, HF 300 W, and 'down to 17Hz' with no upper limit. It does not state the XBD-A or SE designation. The SE retailer copy (17 Hz–25 kHz) is a different revision. Revision is unresolved; driverCount stays unset and no field is stored.
